hypothesis: Value-preserving streaming refinements do not add observations of failure-path resource lifetime. Compose an existing buffered decoding-error test with a source closure postcondition under an explicit total-close issue contract.
scope: Bounded Python HTTPX adapter. Infer one issue-named semantic iterator; no task/repository/witness-ID conditions.
input_policy: Original repository source tests, matching frontend source bytes, and public issue only. Historical cohort contributes only17 trial IDs and original source snapshot paths.
proof_obligations: Issue states consumption and closure for streamed iteration without a success-only qualifier.
Base has one unaliased response and one fully consumed semantic iterator under an existing DecodingError expectation.
All constructor arguments except body representation are closed and identical to a successful streaming donor.
Donor source close-state observer follows list exhaustion or an observed StopIteration, with no explicit close or receiver alias.
New content generator concatenates to the exact original body bytes.
Retain the entire original test, its exception block and suffix; append only the renamed close-state assertion.
selection: Fixed source retrieval rank, path and position; first16 candidates per trial; first controlled native failure stops the trial even if its repeat does not confirm.
execution: All source controls and exact body transport required. Two independent native failures required for an alert. Full-test audit remains evaluator-only.
limitations: The implementation covers one HTTP resource adapter, not all callback or iterator APIs.
The source relation does not remove the need to audit all emitted full tests.
A closed constructor mismatch leads to abstention, including invalid charset or media type setups.
decision: The added close-state observation exposes a valid failure-path resource leak that byte-only refinements did not detect. Keep standalone coverage1/17 separate from round37 hybrid coverage.
recognizer_limitation: The conditional close clause in another issue is followed by a semicolon. The sentence-level matcher does not recognize it. This is an implementation abstention, not evidence that the contract is absent.
